Diego —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the CSV. We pulled the file and ran it against our CRM. Two things jumped out:
1) Only 18 of the 62 leads match our MQL criteria (we require company size >= 50 + verified email domain).
2) Several demo requests in your export were duplicated in our system from the conference app feed (we show those as partner-sourced, not sponsor-sourced).

Because the sponsorship SLA guarantees "40 marketing-qualified leads credited to the sponsor", we need a reconciliation that shows how you derived the 42 MQL count and the specific dedupe/matching rules.

Can you provide the raw timestamps and IP/capture source fields and your exact dedupe keys? If we can't reconcile to at least 40 jointly, we'll need to escalate to procurement to discuss the crediting adjustment per section 4.2 of the sponsorship terms.

Alicia

FinPulse

Hi all —

I pulled the export and ran our dedupe/match script (same process we use for trade shows). Notes below:
- Matching keys: email address exact match; when missing, match on phone + company domain.
- We flagged 9 leads as duplicates of app-sourced contacts (those are marked in column "source_override").
- Of the remaining 53 unique contacts, 42 met our outbound qualification where LeadScore >=30 (score calc attached in column "lead_score_components"). The difference vs. your 18 likely comes from company size: we pull public company size from Clearbit and apply a soft threshold (>=25 FTE) for MQL. FinPulse applies >=50.

Proposed reconciliation steps:
1) Attach the raw timestamps and source id (done) and a clear mapping of our dedupe logic (see Drive link).
2) Run a mutual-match with FinPulse's CRM export (Alicia, if you drop your CSV to the Drive link I can run a join with our dedupe keys).
3) For contract crediting: suggest we use a 2-step approach — first-pass marketing credit based on sponsor-captured unique contacts (we count 42), then a second-pass mutual reconciliation where FinPulse's stricter company-size filter can reduce credited MQLs and we apply an invoice credit proportionally.

I uploaded the join-ready file to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/marketing/events/finpulse-2026/finpulse-mqls.csv

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call to resolve and avoid procurement escalation.

Thanks,
Marissa
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi team —

Thanks Marissa for the clear breakdown. For context on the sponsorship contract: the SLA language calls for "40 MQLs credited to sponsor" but doesn't strictly define the company-size backstop beyond "qualified by standard vendor filters". Given the ambiguity, my recommendation for a quick commercial resolution:
- We agree to a negotiated split: count 42 sponsor-captured MQLs on our side, FinPulse retains right to its own stricter filter.
- For invoice purposes, we propose to net the overlap after mutual-match and if mutual-credited MQLs < 40 we offer a pro-rated sponsor credit of $250 per missing MQL up to a maximum of $10,000.

Operationally Marissa — please run the mutual-match and share the joined file. Alicia — if you can confirm acceptance of the pro-rata credit approach we can close the loop this week.

Karthik
